note: Hilti France tests selling indirectly through a new French retail concept (La Plateforme du Batiment) and then faces a similar opportunity with Home Depot in the US. A channel test in one country used to inform a decision in another: what transfers, what does not?
course_use: Case discussion (channel test in one country, decision in another). Paid via IMD/The Case Centre/HBP (price not shown); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Unilever in Brazil 1997-2007: Marketing Strategies for Low-Income Consumers
author_source: Pierre Chandon, Pedro Pacheco Guimaraes; INSEAD, 2004, case 5188 (24 pp.)
note: Should Unilever divert money from premium brands to low-income consumers in Northeast Brazil, and with a new brand or an extension? Abstract does not describe a formal test; use it as a design exercise: plan a regional test market in the Northeast (price, pack size, distribution) and define cannibalisation metrics.
course_use: Case discussion plus test-design exercise. Paid, about EUR 7 via INSEAD Publishing (also Ivey/Case Centre); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Uber: Competing as Market Leader in the US versus Being a Distant Second in China
author_source: Jochen Wirtz, Christopher Tang; case in Wirtz/Lovelock Services Marketing case collection (hosted by NUS / author site)
note: Uber flopped in China despite strong results elsewhere (Didi 1m+ drivers in 360 cities vs. Uber about 100k in 20 cities). Discussion: what can and cannot be learned from home-market experiments when entering a market with a strong local rival; how city-level launches serve as experiments.
course_use: Case discussion; free PDF on author site.

title: Gillette's Shave India Movement: Razor Sharp against the Stubble
author_source: Singapore Management University case series
note: Adapting Mach3/Guard product and marketing to Indian shaving habits. Use to contrast ethnographic research and in-market testing for emerging-market product design (Gillette Guard launched 2010 at about Rs 15).
course_use: Case discussion. Paid via SMU Case Centre (price not checked); WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Nescafe Classic 70th Anniversary Tin (A)
author_source: IMD, 2014, case study
note: Launch failure of a commemorative tin; the case notes that even cursory consumer testing would likely have uncovered the problems. Short cautionary case for why a small market test or pre-test is cheap insurance.
course_use: Warm-up / cautionary case. Paid via IMD/The Case Centre; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Jumia Group: Africa's First Unicorn
author_source: ICMR (IBS Case Development Centre, India), 2018, case LDEN132, teaching note available
note: Rocket Internet-style copy-build-sell model rolled out across African countries with poor infrastructure and low trust. Discussion: country sequencing as experimentation (launching lighter businesses first, Uganda served from Kenya before local offices), and growth vs. profitability.
course_use: Case discussion (multi-country roll-out, Rocket Internet model). Paid via ICMR/The Case Centre; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Tesco in the United States (Fresh & Easy)
author_source: ICMR (IBS Case Development Centre), 2008, case BSTR291
note: Tesco's Fresh & Easy US entry: intensive consumer research (executives living with American families), first store Nov 2007, openings paused April 2008 after 61 stores. Teaching question: research and test stores vs. a controlled market test with clear stop rules; why did pre-launch research not predict the outcome?
course_use: Case discussion (market-entry test design, failure). Paid via ICMR; no teaching note listed; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Spotify: Price Discrimination
author_source: ICMR (IBS Case Development Centre), case ECON085
note: Freemium pricing and price discrimination (incl. across countries) as Spotify's growth engine. Pair with the 2025 Spotify Lite/Standard/Platinum test in five emerging markets and its partial rollback (examples) to discuss price experiments by country.
course_use: Case discussion (country pricing). Paid via ICMR; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Carrefour in Asia (A): Taiwan - A Bridgehead into Asia
author_source: INSEAD Publishing, case (prize-winning)
note: Taiwan used as a bridgehead/learning market before wider Asian expansion. Good for the lead-market and test-country concept in retail internationalisation: what can a first foreign market teach you and how to formalise that learning.
course_use: Case discussion (bridgehead/lead market). Paid via INSEAD/The Case Centre; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Internationalization Strategy of Manner: Market Entry Brazil
author_source: WU Vienna case (registered with The Case Centre), WU research portal
note: WU case on Austrian confectioner Manner entering Brazil. Not an experimentation case as such; use as a local (Austrian) setting for an exercise: design a pilot/test-market plan (city, channel, price points, success metrics) before a full Brazil entry.
course_use: Case discussion plus test-market design exercise; WU-internal case, check availability via WU or The Case Centre.

title: Booking.com localisation blackout experiment across 45 languages
author_source: DeepL blog summarising New Fluency podcast with Mik Szajna (Head of Localisation, Booking.com), updated 2026, interview write-up
note: Booking.com switched off localised content for a small share of users in all 45 languages for several weeks and compared them to users seeing the localised product; effect described as really significant (can't read, won't buy). No figures given. Great for discussing holdout tests to value localisation (and the ethics/cost of holdouts).
course_use: Example / warm-up for localisation ROI. Free.

title: Wikimedia Fundraising 2015-16 Report: localised banner tests
author_source: Wikimedia Foundation, Meta-Wiki, 2016, fundraising report
note: 2,086 banner tests in one year. Of 10 statistically significant localised-copy tests, 8 increased donations per impression; naming the country in the first line (e.g. Today we ask those of you in Malaysia...) made donating 11% more likely on desktop. Japanese readers found copy read like a translation. Strong example that localisation should be tested, not assumed.
course_use: Example for lecture or exercise (localised copy tests). Free.

title: Wikimedia Fundraising 2013-14: banner A/B testing in about 100 countries and 50 languages
author_source: Wikimedia Foundation, Meta-Wiki, 2014, fundraising report
note: Testing expanded to about 100 countries and 50 languages, with country campaigns of roughly two weeks each and 800+ banners tested worldwide; best English messages adapted by volunteer translators. Shows how to scale a test programme across languages.
course_use: Example (scaling tests across languages). Free.

title: Language learning for the next billion: Duolingo in India
author_source: Duolingo blog, company blog post
note: Market-specific A/B tests in India: placing English-for-Hindi-speakers at top of list (+2% DAU), using English words for language/level in Hindi onboarding (+1% onboarding completion), removing early Plus promotion (+1% DAU), removing Duolingo Plus entirely in India and some Asian countries (+6% DAU). Excellent for discussing country-specific monetisation trade-offs.
course_use: Example / discussion: grow first or monetise first in a new market? Free.

title: Netflix tests paid sharing (extra member) in Chile, Costa Rica and Peru
author_source: 1News NZ, 17 March 2022, news report on Netflix blog post by Chengyi Long
note: Netflix trialled charging for accounts shared outside the household in three Latin American countries (e.g. USD 2.99 in Costa Rica, 2,380 CLP in Chile, 7.9 PEN in Peru) before global roll-out in 2023. Discussion: why small Latin American markets as test countries, what metrics (churn, sign-ups, revenue), and spillovers via press coverage.
course_use: Example (test countries for pricing/policy changes). Free.

title: Netflix tests mobile-only plan in Malaysia and India (2018-2019)
author_source: MediaNama, March 2019, news report
note: Rs 250/month SD mobile-only plan (half of the entry tier) tested with selected users in India after a Malaysia trial in Nov 2018; rolled out in India in July 2019. Classic emerging-market price/package test with low pay-TV ARPU context.
course_use: Example (price/package test in emerging markets). Free.

title: Instagram tests hiding like counts in seven countries (2019)
author_source: PetaPixel, 18 July 2019, news report
note: Test started in Canada (May 2019), expanded to Australia, Brazil, Ireland, Italy, Japan and New Zealand, then some US users (Nov 2019). Illustrates country-level feature tests and the choice of culturally diverse test markets.
course_use: Example / warm-up (selecting test countries). Free.

title: X (Twitter) tests 1 USD per year Not A Bot subscription in New Zealand and the Philippines
author_source: NBC News, October 2023, news report
note: New web users in NZ (NZD 1.43/yr) and the Philippines (PHP 42.51/yr) had to pay to post. Unclear why these two markets were chosen; good prompt for discussing test-market representativeness (high-income vs. emerging, English-speaking) and the stated goal (bots) vs. revenue metrics.
course_use: Example / discussion question. Free.

title: YouTube Premium Lite pilot in Benelux and the Nordics (2021)
author_source: The Next Web, 2 August 2021, news report
note: Cheaper ad-free tier (EUR 6.99 vs. about EUR 11.99) piloted in Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway and Sweden. A European regional price/tier experiment; discuss cannibalisation and why small, high-income European markets are chosen.
course_use: Example (European price-tier test). Free.

title: Twitter Fleets: tested in Brazil, Italy, India and South Korea before global launch (2020)
author_source: The Next Web, 29 July 2020, news report
note: Ephemeral posts first tested in Brazil (March 2020), then Italy, India and South Korea; global launch Nov 2020 (later discontinued). Shows sequential country tests and that a positive test does not guarantee long-run success.
course_use: Example (sequential country tests, long-term effects). Free.

title: Uber cash payments: Hyderabad pilot (2015) expanded to 10 countries
author_source: TechCrunch, 8 February 2016, news report
note: Uber's first global cash pilot in Hyderabad (May 2015), rolled out slowly per city, expanded to India, most of Southeast Asia, Kenya, Nigeria, parts of the Middle East and Peru. Uber reported exponential sign-up growth but gave no numbers. Example of a city pilot for an emerging-market adaptation (low card ownership).
course_use: Example (city pilot as test market; payment localisation). Free.

title: Disney+ technology trial in the Netherlands before global launch (2019)
author_source: Disney+ press release, September 2019
note: Free early trial in the Netherlands from 12 Sept 2019 with a limited library, framed as a technology trial, converting to paid (EUR 6.99) on 12 Nov. Netherlands chosen for high broadband and SVOD penetration. Soft launch outside games.
course_use: Example (soft launch / technical test market). Free.

title: Pokemon GO field tests: Japan, then Australia and New Zealand (2016)
author_source: Android Police, 8 April 2016, news report
note: Niantic field-tested in Japan (March 2016), expanded to Australia and New Zealand, public launch July 2016 in US, AU, NZ. Example of staged technical/market tests and why ANZ are popular test markets.
course_use: Example / warm-up. Free.

title: Brawl Stars vs. Clash Royale: Supercell soft launches in Canada
author_source: Sensor Tower blog, 2017, market-intelligence analysis
note: In Canada, Clash Royale grossed about USD 2.2m in its 57-day soft launch vs. about USD 180k for Brawl Stars over the same period. Supercell uses Canada as US proxy and kills games that miss targets (e.g. Spooky Pop). Good data point for test-market go/kill decisions.
course_use: Example with numbers for class discussion. Free.

title: Supercell soft-launches Clash Mini in Finland, Canada, Sweden, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland
author_source: PocketGamer.biz, news report
note: Choice of Nordic countries plus Canada (and Switzerland) as soft-launch markets. Discuss criteria for test-country choice: similarity to target markets, cost per install, language, platform mix.
course_use: Example. Free.

title: The mobile game soft launch: what to measure and where
author_source: Joshua Lu, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), 17 October 2023, practitioner guide
note: Canada as proxy for US launch; low-cost geographies to stress-test servers and low-spec Android devices. Metrics: crash rates, FTUE completion, D1-D30 retention, DAU/MAU, payer conversion (about 2% casual, 5% midcore), CPI vs LTV. Caveat: no market fully represents a global launch.
course_use: Reading / example (test-market metrics). Free.

title: Test market considerations: countries, timeline, UA and more
author_source: Game Developer (gamedeveloper.com), sponsored practitioner article
note: Practitioner overview of which countries games use as test markets (CANZ as US/UK proxies, Philippines for cheap volume/technical tests), timelines and user acquisition. Sponsored content; use critically.
course_use: Background reading for soft-launch discussion. Free.

title: Coca-Cola Life piloted in Argentina and Chile before Europe
author_source: FoodNavigator, 11 June 2014, trade news
note: Stevia-sweetened Coke first piloted in Argentina (June 2013) and Chile (Nov 2013), then Sweden and the UK (2014); withdrawn from the UK in 2017. Lead/test markets in Latin America for a global product, and a reminder that test success does not guarantee success elsewhere.
course_use: Example (test markets for FMCG). Free.

title: McDonald's McPlant nuggets: nine-restaurant Stuttgart test, then roll-out to 1,400+ German restaurants
author_source: Fox Business, February 2023, news report
note: Germany chosen as first market for plant-based nuggets co-developed with Beyond Meat; limited test in nine Stuttgart-area restaurants preceded national roll-out; further markets depend on demand. DACH example of regional menu tests.
course_use: Example (regional menu test in Germany). Free.

title: Testmarkt Hassloch: Germany's model town for product tests (GfK, 1986-2021)
author_source: Goethe-Institut magazine, feature article (German)
note: GfK tested new products in seven supermarkets in Hassloch (about 20,000 inhabitants) chosen to mirror German households; panel households used scanned cards; a test took 4-6 months and cost at least EUR 50,000. GfK closed it at end of 2021 in favour of apps and online panels. Classic controlled test market vs. today's digital experiments.
course_use: Example / warm-up (classic test market, DACH). Free, German.

title: Deutsche Marktforschung: Hassloch nicht mehr Testmarkt
author_source: ORF.at, 2021, news report (German)
note: Austrian news report on the end of the Hassloch test market. Pair with the Goethe feature to discuss why physical test markets are being replaced by digital and online experiments.
course_use: Short reading (German). Free.

title: Austria as an ideal test market for the German-speaking region
author_source: iTrade News (Czech trade portal), interview with Bettina Kirnbauer (Austrian Business Agency)
note: Investment-promotion view of Austria as DACH test market (manageable size, cultural closeness to Germany; long seen as test market for mobile telecoms). Advocacy source, not evidence; useful for a critical discussion of whether Austria is representative of Germany.
course_use: Discussion prompt (Is Austria a good test market for Germany?). Free.

title: Does Machine Translation Affect International Trade? Evidence from eBay
author_source: Erik Brynjolfsson, Xiang Hui, Meng Liu; NBER WP 24917 / Management Science 65(12), 2019
note: eBay's introduction of machine translation for listings (English-Spanish first) raised US exports to Spanish-speaking Latin America by 17.5% (NBER abstract; MIT press coverage reports 10.9% more trade between affected country pairs). Shows language as a cross-border trade barrier and how a staged roll-out enables causal estimates.
course_use: Example / reading (localisation as treatment). NBER WP free for many; journal version WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Will a Five-Minute Discussion Change Your Mind? A Countrywide Experiment on Voter Choice in France
author_source: Vincent Pons; American Economic Review, 2018
note: Hollande 2012 campaign randomised door-to-door canvassing across 4,674 precincts (about 5 million voters): no turnout effect but +3.2 pts vote share in round 1 and +2.8 in round 2; effects persisted. A European counterpart to Obama-style campaign experiments; replication data on openICPSR.
course_use: Example (campaign experiment outside the US). WU-Lizenz prüfen (AER); replication data free.

title: Behavioral Insights for Tax Compliance: Evidence from Guatemala
author_source: Stewart Kettle, Marco Hernandez, Simon Ruda, Michael Sanders; World Bank Policy Research WP 7690 (with UK Behavioural Insights Team), 2016
note: RCT with about 43,000 Guatemalan taxpayers: no letter vs. original letter vs. four behavioural variants. All letters raised declarations; only two (deliberate-choice framing, social norm) raised payments; about USD 760k extra revenue, 36x the cost. Shows transfer of UK nudge letters to a Latin American context.
course_use: Example (transferring nudges across countries). Free.

title: Applying Behavioral Insights to Improve Tax Collection: Experimental Evidence from Poland
author_source: Hernandez, Jamison, Korczyc, Mazar, Sormani; World Bank eMBeD, 2017, policy brief / working paper
note: RCT with 149,925 Polish taxpayers who filed but missed payment: default letter vs. nine behaviourally worded letters, outcomes at 4, 7 and 13 weeks. Behavioural letters significantly improved compliance. Pair with the Guatemala trial: same idea, different country, different winning messages.
course_use: Example / comparison exercise across countries. Free.

title: Behavioural Insights Team: Global Innovation Fund programme (Guatemala, Bangladesh, Indonesia)
author_source: Global Innovation Fund, investment profile
note: BIT worked with 12 partners in six countries, starting 39 projects and completing 23 randomised evaluations; Indonesian tax trials reached 11m+ taxpayers. Example of scaling an RCT approach from the UK to emerging markets.
course_use: Example (scaling experimentation internationally). Free.

title: Behavioural Insights and Public Policy: Lessons from Around the World
author_source: OECD, 2017, report with 100+ case studies
note: Over 100 applications of behavioural insights, many tested by RCTs, across OECD member and partner countries (consumer protection, energy, tax, health). Source bank for country comparisons of the same intervention type.
course_use: Example bank / reading. Free (OECD iLibrary).

title: Insight Austria: behavioural economics unit at IHS Vienna
author_source: Institut fuer Hoehere Studien (IHS), Vienna, research unit website
note: Austria's research unit and nudge unit, testing interventions in experimental studies (led by Katharina Gangl since 2022, previously Martin Kocher). Local source for Austrian field experiments and possible guest speakers.
course_use: Local example / guest-speaker lead. Free.

title: Meta white paper: partnership ads in EMEA conversion lift studies
author_source: Relevant Audience, summary of Meta white paper, 2026, practitioner news
note: Across 20 conversion lift studies by EMEA advertisers (H1 2025), campaigns with at least 30% partnership (creator) ads had 45% lower median cost per incremental purchase. Company-supplied, 92% confidence level. Use to discuss multi-country lift meta-analyses and vendor-reported evidence.
course_use: Example for critical discussion of platform lift studies. Free.

title: Scaling search lift methodologies with Meta (13 EMEA conversion lift studies)
author_source: Journey Further, agency insight article
note: Meta meta-analysis of 13 EMEA lift studies (Apr-Oct 2024): about 13% incremental organic searches and 14% incremental paid searches among exposed audiences (wide 90% credible intervals). Example of cross-channel lift measured across European markets.
course_use: Example (cross-channel lift, Europe). Free.

title: The Value of Pop-Up Stores on Retailing Platforms: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Alibaba
author_source: Management Science, 2019/2020, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2019.3410
note: Randomised experiment with about 800,000 Alibaba customers: a message about a Tmall pop-up event raised foot traffic and later spending at participating retailers' Tmall stores. Chinese platform field experiment linking online and offline.
course_use: Example (field experiments on Chinese platforms). WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Price promotions field experiment on Alibaba with 100m+ customers (cart-based discounts)
author_source: Zhang, Dai, Dong et al.; Management Science, 2020, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2019.3316
note: Randomised experiment with over 100 million customers and 11,000 retailers; cart-based discounts roughly doubled same-day sales of promoted products but had unintended longer-term effects. Scale of experimentation in Chinese e-commerce.
course_use: Example (promotion experiments at scale, China). WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Value of Personal Data in Internet Commerce: A High-Stakes Field Experiment on Data Regulation Policy (Alibaba)
author_source: Management Science, 2023, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2023.4828
note: Random subset of 555,800 Alibaba customers had personal data removed from homepage recommendations; engagement and sales dropped sharply, especially for niche merchants. Useful for discussing how differing privacy regimes (GDPR vs. China) change what can be tested and personalised by market.
course_use: Example (privacy regulation and experimentation across regimes). WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Measuring consumer price elasticity for mobile money services (Tanzania RCT)
author_source: AEA RCT Registry, trial 14284, registered field experiment
note: Households randomised to 50% or 100% discounts on some mobile-money transactions for 8 weeks vs. control to estimate willingness to pay. Pricing experiment design in an emerging market; pair with the M-Pesa pricing case.
course_use: Example (price experiment design, Africa). Free.

title: Spotify tests Lite/Standard/Platinum tiers in five emerging markets, then scales back
author_source: Music In Africa, 2025/2026, news report
note: Three-tier Premium structure launched Nov 2025 in India, Indonesia, UAE, Saudi Arabia and South Africa; later Lite removed and Standard prices lowered back while Platinum retained (prices raised in some markets). Example of a multi-market price-architecture test and partial rollback.
course_use: Example (country price tests and reversals). Free.

title: Rethinking the Oreo for Chinese consumers
author_source: NPR (via KUNC), 27 January 2012, radio feature
note: Kraft's US Oreo underperformed in China; consumer research and taste tests with hundreds of Chinese consumers led to a less sweet, smaller reformulation that became China's top-selling cookie. Product testing for local adaptation (sources disagree on timeline and prototype counts).
course_use: Warm-up example (local product testing). Free.

title: How Gillette innovated and improved its market share in India
author_source: Business Today (India), LBS case study series, 2014, magazine case
note: Gillette Guard: first razor designed just for India, launched Oct 2010 at Rs 15, after a team observed Indian men shaving. Example of local research and testing behind emerging-market product design (reverse innovation).
course_use: Example / pre-reading for Gillette SMU case. Free.

title: On the Effectiveness of Online Marketing (Zalando)
author_source: Zalando Engineering Blog, February 2019, company blog
note: Zalando post on measuring incremental effects of online marketing, citing Google's geo-experiment methodology; Zalando/Lounge job ads describe geo-experiments and synthetic control across 20+ European countries. Details on country design not visible in search snippet; read before using.
course_use: Example (European marketing incrementality). Free.

title: Global Market Scoping Test: a retailer tests 13 international markets over six months
author_source: Locaria, agency case study
note: Vendor case describing a six-month test in which a retailer entered 13 international markets in parallel to compare which offered the biggest opportunity. Example of using parallel market tests for market selection; vendor source, results not independently verified.
course_use: Example for discussing parallel market tests in market selection. Free.

title: synthdid (R) - synthetic difference-in-differences
author_source: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens & Wager; GitHub synth-inference
note: R package (GitHub only, not on CRAN; BSD-3 licence). Combines synthetic control unit weights with DiD time weights; ships the California Prop 99 state panel. Ideal for estimating the effect of a launch in one or a few countries/states against a weighted donor pool of untreated markets, with placebo/jackknife SEs.
course_use: Lab: estimate a single-country campaign effect with SDID vs. SCM vs. DiD; install via remotes::install_github.

title: augsynth (R) - augmented synthetic control, incl. staggered adoption
author_source: Ben-Michael, Feller & Rothstein; GitHub ebenmichael/augsynth
note: R package (GitHub, MIT licence). Ridge-augmented SCM corrects imperfect pre-treatment fit; multisynth() handles staggered adoption, i.e. markets entering treatment at different dates - the typical country-by-country rollout pattern.
course_use: Lab/project: staggered multi-country launch analysis with multisynth.

title: Synth (R) - classic synthetic control method
author_source: Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller; CRAN
note: CRAN v1.1-10, GPL (>=2). Reference implementation of SCM with the Basque Country example; the same authors' German reunification study is the textbook cross-country SCM case (West Germany vs. OECD donors).
course_use: Lab: replicate a cross-country synthetic control before moving to modern variants.

title: fect (R) - fixed effects counterfactual estimators / gsynth
author_source: Liu, Wang & Xu; CRAN
note: CRAN v2.4.5, MIT. Interactive fixed effects, matrix completion and generalized synthetic control (gsynth merged into fect) for panels with many treated units and staggered treatment; built-in placebo and equivalence pre-trend tests.
course_use: Project: country x month panel with treatment switching on in different markets; parallel-trend diagnostics.

title: CausalPy (PyMC Labs)
author_source: PyMC Labs; PyPI
note: PyPI v0.9.0, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.11. Bayesian (PyMC) and sklearn back-ends for synthetic control, geo-lift, DiD, interrupted time series and regression discontinuity; returns the full posterior of the lift per market. Python counterpart to GeoLift/augsynth.
course_use: Lab: Bayesian geo-lift for one country vs. donor countries in a Jupyter notebook.

title: scpi (R/Python/Stata) - synthetic control prediction intervals
author_source: Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba & Titiunik; nppackages
note: CRAN v4.0.1 / PyPI scpi_pkg v4.0.0, GPL-3. Prediction intervals for synthetic control with multiple treated units and staggered adoption - answers the usual 'SCM has no standard errors' objection in market-level studies.
course_use: Lab/background: add valid uncertainty to a single-market launch estimate.

title: SparseSC (Microsoft) - sparse synthetic controls
author_source: Microsoft Research; GitHub
note: Python package (GitHub, MIT; not on PyPI). Penalised synthetic control with feature/donor selection; designed for many units and covariates, e.g. choosing comparable markets from a large set of regions.
course_use: Optional advanced lab; install from GitHub.

title: did (R) - Callaway & Sant'Anna staggered DiD
author_source: Callaway & Sant'Anna; CRAN
note: CRAN v2.5.1, GPL-3. Group-time ATTs and event-study aggregation for staggered adoption; avoids the negative-weight bias of two-way fixed effects when countries adopt a feature or campaign at different times.
course_use: Lab: country rollout panel -> group-time ATT -> event-study plot.

title: fixest (R) - fast fixed effects incl. Sun-Abraham estimator
author_source: Berge; CRAN
note: CRAN v0.14.2, GPL-3. High-dimensional fixed effects (market, week), multiway clustered SEs and sunab() interaction-weighted event study for staggered rollouts.
course_use: Lab: market x time regressions with clustering by country.

title: pyfixest (Python)
author_source: Fischer et al.; PyPI
note: PyPI v0.60.0, MIT, Python >=3.10. Python port of fixest: fixed-effects OLS/Poisson, cluster-robust and wild-bootstrap inference, DiD/event-study estimators, plus Romano-Wolf and Bonferroni corrections across outcomes.
course_use: Lab (Python track): staggered market rollouts and Romano-Wolf across many market-level estimates.

title: differences (Python) - staggered DiD
author_source: Dionisi; PyPI
note: PyPI v0.3.0, GPL-3, Python >=3.10. Python implementation of Callaway & Sant'Anna ATT(g,t) with aggregation and plotting.
course_use: Lab: Python alternative to the R did package.

title: DIDmultiplegtDYN (R/Stata)
author_source: de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille; CRAN
note: CRAN v2.4.0, MIT. Event-study DiD robust to heterogeneous and dynamic effects; allows treatments switching on and off (e.g. promotions toggled by country).
course_use: Advanced lab for non-absorbing treatments across markets.

title: metafor (R) - meta-analysis
author_source: Viechtbauer; CRAN
note: CRAN v5.2-1, GPL (>=2). Fixed/random-effects and meta-regression models; pool per-country experiment effects, estimate between-market heterogeneity (tau^2, I^2) and test moderators such as region or cultural distance.
course_use: Lab: meta-analyse the same A/B test run in 10 countries; forest plot by market.

title: brms (R) - Bayesian multilevel models via Stan
author_source: Buerkner; CRAN
note: CRAN v2.23.0, GPL-2. lme4-style formulas for hierarchical models, e.g. conversion ~ treatment + (1 + treatment | country), giving partially pooled country-level lifts with shrinkage for small markets.
course_use: Lab: no pooling vs. complete pooling vs. partial pooling of country effects.

title: baggr (R) - Bayesian aggregator for multi-site experiments
author_source: Wiecek & Meager; CRAN
note: CRAN v0.8.2, GPL (>=3). Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis built for aggregating RCTs across sites (Meager microcredit study); works from summary effects or individual data, with leave-one-site-out and pooling diagnostics.
course_use: Lab: 'should we trust the German result for Austria?' - predictive effect for a new market.

title: DoubleML (Python/R)
author_source: Bach, Chernozhukov, Kurz & Spindler; PyPI
note: PyPI v0.11.4, BSD-3 (R version on CRAN). Double/debiased ML for ATE, interactive regression models, group average treatment effects (GATE) and CATE; estimate effect differences by country with flexible controls.
course_use: Lab: GATE by country on an experiment dataset.

title: randomizr (R) - block and cluster randomisation
author_source: Coppock; CRAN (DeclareDesign family)
note: CRAN v2.0.1, MIT. block_ra() stratifies by country, cluster_ra() assigns whole regions/markets, block_and_cluster_ra() does both; returns assignment probabilities for correct analysis.
course_use: Lab: randomise stores/regions within countries with reproducible code.

title: DeclareDesign (R) - design declaration and diagnosis
author_source: Blair, Coppock, Cooper & Humphreys; CRAN
note: CRAN v2.0.0, MIT. Simulates a full design (population, assignment, estimator) to diagnose power, bias and coverage - e.g. individual vs. cluster-by-market randomisation, pooled vs. per-country estimands.
course_use: Project: pre-register and diagnose a multi-country experiment before fielding.

title: blockTools (R) - blocking and matched pairs
author_source: Moore & Schnakenberg; CRAN
note: CRAN v0.6-6, GPL. Builds blocks/matched pairs on covariates (market size, baseline sales), randomises within blocks and checks balance - for pairing similar regions in geo tests.
course_use: Lab: matched-pair design of 20 regions.

title: semTools + lavaan (R) - measurement invariance testing
author_source: Jorgensen et al.; Rosseel; CRAN
note: semTools CRAN v0.5-10, lavaan v0.7-3, GPL (>=2). measEq.syntax() tests configural/metric/scalar invariance across country groups - needed before comparing survey-experiment outcome scales across cultures.
course_use: Lab: invariance of a purchase-intention scale in a 3-country survey experiment.

title: generalizeR (R) - generalising experiments to target populations
author_source: Tipton et al.; GitHub NUstat
note: R package (GitHub). Stratified recruitment and Tipton's generalizability index to assess how well an experimental sample represents a target population - transfers to 'does our pilot-market sample resemble the roll-out market?'.
course_use: Advanced lab on external validity.

title: inferference (R) - causal effects under interference
author_source: Saul & Hudgens; CRAN
note: CRAN v1.0.3, GPL (>=2). IPW estimators of direct, indirect (spillover), total and overall effects under group-level interference - relevant when markets spill over (cross-border shopping, shared media).
course_use: Advanced methods session illustrating spillover vs. direct effects.

title: Meridian (Google) - geo-level hierarchical Bayesian MMM
author_source: Google; GitHub
note: PyPI google-meridian v2.1.0, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.10. Geo-hierarchical MMM that uses geo-experiment/lift results as ROI priors; shows how multi-region experiments feed into planning across markets.
course_use: Background/project: calibrate a multi-geo MMM with lift-test results.

title: Kameleoon - EU-based experimentation platform
author_source: Kameleoon (France)
note: Commercial web/feature experimentation platform headquartered in France with EU data hosting and consent-management integrations. Case for discussing data residency and how consent rates shrink/bias experiment samples per country.
course_use: Background/vendor case for platform choice in EU markets.

title: Varify.io - German A/B testing tool
author_source: Varify.io (Germany)
note: German SaaS A/B testing tool with flat-rate pricing positioned on GDPR compliance and EU servers; analysis via GA4/Matomo integrations.
course_use: Background: EU vendor positioning vs. US platforms; possible trial for student projects.

title: Convert Experiences
author_source: Convert.com
note: Commercial A/B testing platform marketed on privacy (GDPR/CCPA, cookieless options); supports geo and language targeting for country-specific variants.
course_use: Background/demo of geo- and language-targeted test setup.

title: Matomo A/B Testing plugin
author_source: Matomo (InnoCraft)
note: Premium plugin for the open-source Matomo analytics (GPL core); runs A/B tests with data on own or EU servers - common in EU public-sector and privacy-sensitive settings.
course_use: Background: privacy-first experimentation stack in the EU.

title: PostHog EU Cloud (data residency)
author_source: PostHog
note: Open-source (MIT core) product analytics with experiments; EU Cloud hosts data in Frankfurt. Complements the existing PostHog Experiments entry with the EU data-residency angle.
course_use: Lab: free tier for student experiments with EU-hosted data.

title: Weglot - website translation (for language-variant tests)
author_source: Weglot (France)
note: Commercial website translation/localisation service creating language subdirectories. Not a testing tool itself; used together with A/B tools to test machine vs. human translation or localised copy per market.
course_use: Project idea: test translated vs. transcreated landing pages.

title: Qualtrics - survey experiments across countries
author_source: Qualtrics
note: Commercial survey platform: Randomizer/block randomisation for vignette and conjoint experiments, multi-language surveys with translation management, panel sourcing in many countries. Check WU institutional access.
course_use: Project: cross-country survey experiment with translated versions.

title: Prolific - participant recruitment with country filters
author_source: Prolific (UK)
note: Participant platform with prescreeners for country of residence, nationality and language; enables quota samples across e.g. UK, US and several European countries. Pay per participant.
course_use: Project: field the same experiment in several countries with comparable samples.

title: oTree - interactive and multi-player experiments
author_source: Chen, Schonger & Wickens; otree.org
note: Open-source Python framework (PyPI otree v6.0.15, MIT) for lab/online experiments incl. interactive games and markets; multi-language apps; integrates with Prolific/MTurk.
course_use: Lab: build a pricing or bargaining experiment run in multiple countries.

title: Gorilla Experiment Builder
author_source: Cauldron (UK)
note: Browser-based no-code experiment builder (reaction-time tasks, questionnaires, randomiser nodes) with localisation and recruitment integrations. Paid per participant or licence.
course_use: Project: cross-cultural behavioural experiments without coding.

title: Labvanced - online behavioural experiments
author_source: Labvanced (Germany)
note: German browser-based experiment platform with EU (GDPR) hosting, webcam eye tracking, multi-language studies and built-in panel recruitment.
course_use: Project: EU-hosted cross-country experiments incl. eye tracking.

title: Cint (incl. Lucid) - global sample exchange
author_source: Cint Group (Sweden)
note: Programmatic access to online respondents in 130+ countries (Cint acquired Lucid in 2021); used to field survey experiments with country quotas.
course_use: Background: sourcing multi-country samples; cost and quality trade-offs.

title: Many Labs 1 (OSF)
author_source: Klein et al. (2014), Social Psychology 45(3)
note: 13 classic effects replicated in 36 samples (~6,300 participants) across 12 countries; site and country identifiers allow per-site effects and cross-national heterogeneity. Open on OSF.
course_use: Lab: meta-analyse an anchoring or framing effect across countries.

title: Many Labs 2 (OSF)
author_source: Klein et al. (2018), AMPPS 1(4)
note: 28 effects in 125 samples from 36 countries/territories (~15,000 participants); built to study variation across samples and cultures (WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD). Raw and cleaned data plus code.
course_use: Lab/project: heterogeneity of effects by country; random-effects meta-analysis.

title: Many Labs 3 (OSF)
author_source: Ebersole et al. (2016), JESP 67
note: Effects tested in 20 sites across the academic semester - analogue for timing/seasonality effects in multi-site experiments.
course_use: Lab: time-of-period moderation of experimental effects.

title: Psychological Science Accelerator (PSA) studies
author_source: Psychological Science Accelerator network
note: Global lab network running studies in dozens of countries (face perception, COVID-19 message framing, gain/loss framing); datasets on OSF with translation and site metadata.
course_use: Project: message/framing experiments across many countries; equivalence issues.

title: AEA RCT Registry
author_source: American Economic Association
note: Registry of 10,000+ randomised trials worldwide, searchable by country and keyword (pricing, marketing, consumer behaviour); pre-analysis plans and links to data.
course_use: Lab: critique pre-registrations of multi-country trials.

title: J-PAL Dataverse
author_source: J-PAL, Harvard Dataverse
note: Replication data for many field RCTs in numerous countries (incl. pricing, information and marketing-type interventions in emerging markets). Licence per study, mostly CC0.
course_use: Project data: re-analyse a field RCT; compare effects across countries.

title: World Bank Microdata Library - Impact Evaluation collection
author_source: World Bank
note: Impact-evaluation surveys (baseline/endline, treatment indicators) from many countries, often cluster-randomised by village/region; access from public use to licensed files.
course_use: Project data: multi-country cluster-randomised designs.

title: 3ie Development Evidence Portal
author_source: International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie)
note: Searchable database of impact evaluations and systematic reviews across low- and middle-income countries; source of effect sizes by country for meta-analysis exercises.
course_use: Lab: collect effect sizes from several countries for a meta-analysis.

title: Expedia Personalize Hotel Search (ICDM 2013, Kaggle)
author_source: Expedia / Kaggle
note: ~10M rows of hotel search impressions with clicks/bookings; random_bool flags searches where results were randomly ordered (built-in experiment); site_id, visitor_location_country_id and prop_country_id allow comparing position effects across point-of-sale markets. Kaggle rules.
course_use: Lab: position effects under random ordering, heterogeneous by visitor country.

title: AliExpress multi-country search dataset (Tianchi)
author_source: Alibaba / AliExpress
note: Search logs with impressions, clicks and purchases from five AliExpress country markets (reportedly NL, ES, FR, US, RU - verify on page). Observational, not randomised; for cross-market funnel comparisons and market-transfer modelling. Tianchi account required.
course_use: Project: compare funnel metrics across countries; why observational data is not an experiment.

title: KuaiRand - recommendation logs with random exposure
author_source: Kuaishou; Gao et al. (2022), CIKM
note: Short-video logs (KuaiRand-27K/1K/Pure) where some items were shown via random exposure - an unbiased randomised slice for off-policy evaluation and debiasing. Single market (China).
course_use: Lab: compare estimates from randomised vs. logged exposure.

title: Ali-CCP (Alibaba Click and Conversion Prediction)
author_source: Alibaba; Ma et al. (2018) ESMM, SIGIR
note: ~85M Taobao recommendation impressions with click and conversion labels (~0.4M users, 4.3M items). Observational (China); classic case of sample-selection bias in CVR - contrast to experimental data. Tianchi registration.
course_use: Background/lab on selection bias vs. randomisation.

title: Taobao display advertising click data
author_source: Alibaba Tianchi
note: ~26M ad impressions/clicks from ~1.14M users over 8 days with user profiles and behaviour logs. Observational, single market. Tianchi registration.
course_use: Lab: CTR baseline; non-experimental contrast.

title: Eurostat Digital economy and society (ICT usage, e-commerce)
author_source: Eurostat
note: Country-level EU indicators (online purchasing, cross-border e-commerce, internet use, privacy behaviour) by year and demographics. Free reuse. Moderators and sizing for cross-market experiments.
course_use: Project: explain cross-country variation in lift with ICT/e-commerce indicators.

title: OECD Data Explorer
author_source: OECD
note: Country panels on ICT access, prices, consumer confidence and household spending; CC BY 4.0. Covariates for country-level meta-regression and donor pools.
course_use: Project: country moderators.

title: World Development Indicators (World Bank DataBank)
author_source: World Bank
note: 1,400+ indicators for ~217 economies since 1960 (GDP per capita, internet users, mobile subscriptions); CC BY 4.0. Predictors for country-level synthetic control.
course_use: Lab: build a country donor pool for SCM.

title: Google Trends
author_source: Google
note: Normalised search interest by country/region and week; pseudo-outcome for geo tests (pre-period fit, placebo tests) and for checking holiday/seasonality differences across markets. Free; pytrends/gtrendsR.
course_use: Lab: compare seasonality across DE/AT/CH to time a test.

title: Statista
author_source: Statista
note: Market and consumer statistics by country (e-commerce penetration, ad spend, channel use). Via WU library licence.
course_use: Background: market sizing and context for multi-country test planning.

title: German reunification synthetic control data
author_source: Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2015), AJPS; Harvard Dataverse
note: Country panel (West Germany + 16 OECD countries, 1960-2003): GDP per capita, trade openness, inflation, industry share, schooling, investment. Canonical cross-country SCM example.
course_use: Lab: SCM with countries as units; leave-one-out donors.

title: California Proposition 99 state panel (bundled in synthdid)
author_source: Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2010), JASA
note: 39 US states x 1970-2000 per-capita cigarette sales; treatment = California tobacco programme from 1989. Bundled as california_prop99. Classic geo panel for SCM/SDID teaching.
course_use: Lab: SCM vs. SDID vs. DiD on the same panel.

title: Rossmann Store Sales (Kaggle)
author_source: Rossmann / Kaggle
note: Daily sales of 1,115 German drugstores (~1M rows) with promo flags, state and school holidays by German federal state, store type and competition. Not an experiment, but a realistic regional panel for simulating geo tests and handling regional holiday calendars. Kaggle rules.
course_use: Lab: simulate a regional promo geo test; adjust for state-specific holidays.

title: M5 Forecasting (Walmart, Kaggle)
author_source: Walmart / University of Nicosia, Kaggle
note: Daily unit sales of 3,049 products in 10 stores across 3 US states (CA, TX, WI), 2011-2016, with prices, events and state-specific SNAP days. Panel for geo-test simulation and power analysis by region.
course_use: Lab: power analysis for a state-level geo test.

title: Global Preferences Survey (GPS)
author_source: Falk, Becker, Dohmen, Enke, Huffman & Sunde (2018), QJE; briq institute
note: ~80,000 respondents in 76 countries measuring time preference, risk taking, reciprocity, altruism and trust; country- and individual-level data downloadable for research. Country moderators for HTE/meta-regression (e.g. risk aversion vs. lift of guarantee messaging).
course_use: Project: explain cross-country variation in experiment effects with preference data.

title: Hofstede cultural dimensions data matrix
author_source: geerthofstede.com
note: Country scores on six cultural dimensions for ~100 countries; free download for academic use. Standard (and contested) moderator for cross-cultural experiment effects.
course_use: Lab: meta-regression of per-country lift on cultural dimensions.

title: European Social Survey (ESS)
author_source: ESS ERIC
note: Biennial cross-national survey (30+ countries) with documented translation (TRAPD) and equivalence procedures and some embedded survey experiments. Free with registration.
course_use: Background/lab: translation and equivalence practice for cross-country experiments.

title: Stratified (blocked) randomisation by country
author_source: Athey & Imbens (2017), The econometrics of randomized experiments, Handbook of Economic Field Experiments Vol. 1
note: Randomise within country (or country x device) strata so each market has balanced arms; analyse with stratum fixed effects or stratum-weighted ATE. Gains precision and supports per-country estimates; chapter also covers clustering and heterogeneity.
course_use: Background reading; lab with randomizr::block_ra.

title: Cluster randomisation by market and clustered inference
author_source: Abadie, Athey, Imbens & Wooldridge (2023), QJE 138(1)
note: When treatment is assigned at market/region level (pricing, TV, local promos), SEs must follow the assignment design; clarifies when to cluster and why few clusters (few countries) limits inference. Pair with wild cluster bootstrap.
course_use: Background; discuss power with only 8-20 markets.

title: Synthetic control for single-market launches
author_source: Abadie (2021), Journal of Economic Literature 59(2)
note: Feasibility, data requirements and placebo inference for synthetic control - the standard approach when a campaign or launch happens in one country and comparison countries are weighted.
course_use: Background; lab with Synth/CausalPy.

title: Synthetic control in cross-country comparative research
author_source: Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller (2015), AJPS 59(2)
note: German reunification application with countries as units; donor-pool choice, placebo inference and leave-one-out robustness for country-level interventions.
course_use: Lab with the reunification dataset.

title: Synthetic difference-in-differences
author_source: Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens & Wager (2021), AER 111(12)
note: Combines unit and time weights; more robust than SCM or DiD alone and works with several treated markets.
course_use: Lab with synthdid.

title: Augmented synthetic control and staggered multisynth
author_source: Ben-Michael, Feller & Rothstein (2021), JASA 116(536)
note: Bias correction when the synthetic control fits poorly; extended to staggered adoption - matching phased country rollouts.
course_use: Advanced lab with augsynth.

title: Difference-in-differences with staggered country rollouts
author_source: Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021), J. of Econometrics 225(2); Goodman-Bacon (2021), same issue
note: Two-way fixed effects can be badly biased when markets adopt at different times and effects vary; group-time ATTs and the Goodman-Bacon decomposition (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.03.014) diagnose and fix this for country-by-country rollouts.
course_use: Lab with did / differences packages.

title: Recent DiD synthesis (staggered timing, parallel trends, few clusters)
author_source: Roth, Sant'Anna, Bilinski & Poe (2023), J. of Econometrics 235(2)
note: Practitioner review of staggered timing, parallel-trends sensitivity and inference with few treated clusters - a checklist for market-level rollouts.
course_use: Background reading for project groups.

title: Randomised paired geo experiments and trimmed match
author_source: Chen & Au (2022), Annals of Applied Statistics 16(1)
note: Pairs similar geos, randomises within pairs and uses a trimmed estimator robust to outlying regions to estimate iROAS; design logic transfers to pairing comparable countries/regions.
course_use: Background to trimmed_match; design exercise.

title: Bayesian hierarchical pooling of experiments across countries
author_source: Meager (2019), AEJ: Applied Economics 11(1)
note: Aggregates seven microcredit RCTs from seven countries with a hierarchical model, separating true heterogeneity from noise and predicting the effect in a new site - template for 'what will this test do in the next market?'.
course_use: Lab with baggr/brms.

title: Partial pooling instead of multiple-comparison corrections
author_source: Gelman, Hill & Yajima (2012), J. of Research on Educational Effectiveness 5(2)
note: Multilevel models handle many group comparisons (e.g. 25 country-level lifts) by shrinking noisy estimates instead of Bonferroni-style corrections.
course_use: Discussion: frequentist vs. Bayesian answers to 'which countries won?'.

title: Multiple hypothesis testing across subgroups/markets (List-Shaikh-Xu)
author_source: List, Shaikh & Xu (2019), Experimental Economics 22
note: Bootstrap FWER control for multiple outcomes, treatments and subgroups (e.g. markets), more powerful than Bonferroni; code available.
course_use: Lab: FWER over per-country results vs. Benjamini-Hochberg.

title: Heterogeneous treatment effects by country with causal forests
author_source: Athey, Tibshirani & Wager (2019), Annals of Statistics 47(2)
note: Generalized random forests (basis of grf); honest causal forests give CATEs with valid confidence intervals; country/market covariates enter as moderators; best linear projection summarises variation by market.
course_use: Lab with grf on a multi-country dataset.

title: Double/debiased machine learning for group effects by market
author_source: Chernozhukov et al. (2018), Econometrics Journal 21(1)
note: Orthogonal ML with cross-fitting for treatment effects with many controls; group average treatment effects by country follow directly.
course_use: Lab with DoubleML.

title: Transportability of experimental results across populations
author_source: Pearl & Bareinboim (2014), Statistical Science 29(4)
note: Selection diagrams formalise when an effect measured in one market can be transported to another and which target-market data are needed - formal backbone for 'test in Germany, roll out in Austria'.
course_use: Background; pilot-market selection discussion.

title: Generalisability of RCT results to a target population
author_source: Stuart, Cole, Bradshaw & Leaf (2011), JRSS A 174(2)
note: Propensity-score measures of similarity between experimental sample and target population, plus reweighting to estimate the target-population effect.
course_use: Lab: reweight a pilot-country sample to a target-country profile.

title: Measurement invariance in cross-national consumer research
author_source: Steenkamp & Baumgartner (1998), Journal of Consumer Research 25(1)
note: Multi-group CFA (configural, metric, scalar) to establish that outcome scales mean the same across countries before comparing experimental effects.
course_use: Lab with lavaan/semTools.

title: Cross-national response styles
author_source: Baumgartner & Steenkamp (2001), Journal of Marketing Research 38(2)
note: Acquiescence, extreme and midpoint responding differ across 11 EU countries and bias scale scores - key threat when survey-experiment outcomes are Likert ratings compared across markets.
course_use: Background; design implications (behavioural outcomes, within-country contrasts).

title: Interference and spillovers between units/markets
author_source: Hudgens & Halloran (2008), JASA 103(482)
note: Direct, indirect, total and overall effects under partial interference and two-stage randomisation - applies to cross-border spillovers and choosing market clusters.
course_use: Advanced methods; inferference package.

title: Multi-site designs to study variation across countries
author_source: Klein et al. (2018), Many Labs 2, AMPPS 1(4)
note: Standardised protocol, translation and site-level analysis for one experiment in 36 countries; separates cross-cultural heterogeneity from sampling error.
course_use: Background; pairs with Many Labs 2 data.

title: Power and optimal design for multisite (multi-market) trials
author_source: Raudenbush & Liu (2000), Psychological Methods 5(2)
note: Power depends on number of sites, sample per site and effect heterogeneity; formalises the trade-off between more countries vs. more users per country.
course_use: Lab: power planning for a 5- vs. 15-market test.

title: John A. List
author_source: University of Chicago, Kenneth C. Griffin Professor of Economics; former Chief Economist at Uber, Lyft and Walmart; academic/practitioner; Global
note: Pioneer of natural field experiments in markets, many run in several countries; theory of scaling and why effects shrink when moved to new populations (voltage drop). Directly relevant to the external validity of marketing experiments across markets. Presents in English. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Recorded talks and podcast interviews on scaling and field experiments (EN) for a session on external validity; a live guest lecture is unrealistic, a remote Q&A is possible at best.

title: Stefano DellaVigna
author_source: UC Berkeley, Professor of Economics and Business Administration; academic; Global
note: Co-author of RCTs to Scale (Econometrica 2022, with Elizabeth Linos): 126 nudge-unit trials with 23 million people show effects about one-sixth of those in academic journals, mainly because of publication bias. Also runs forecasting of experimental results (Social Science Prediction Platform). EN.
course_use: Shows students why published effect sizes overstate what they will see when rolling out in a new market; use his paper and talks in the external validity session; remote talk possible.

title: Eva Vivalt
author_source: University of Toronto, Assistant Professor of Economics; affiliated with J-PAL; academic; Global
note: How Much Can We Generalize from Impact Evaluations? (JEEA 2020): 15,024 estimates from 635 papers; a result from one study predicts the sign in a similar study only about 61 percent of the time. Works on how decision-makers interpret evidence and with DellaVigna on forecasting results. EN.
course_use: Core reading and speaker on whether a test from one country transfers to another; the 80,000 Hours podcast interview works as a pre-class listen; remote guest Q&A (EN).

title: Rachael Meager
author_source: Economist working on Bayesian aggregation of experiments (previously London School of Economics); academic; Global
note: Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of multi-site experiments (microcredit RCTs across seven countries, AEJ Applied 2019) to separate true cross-site heterogeneity from noise. A model for pooling A/B tests across markets. EN. Rolle prüfen (affiliation may have changed; her personal site is a placeholder).
course_use: Methods input on partial pooling of country-level test results; recorded seminar or remote talk (EN).

title: Elias Bareinboim
author_source: Columbia University, Associate Professor of Computer Science, Director of the Causal Artificial Intelligence Lab; academic; Global
note: With Judea Pearl, developed transportability theory (Statistical Science 2014; PNAS 2016 on data fusion): when and how an experimental effect from one population can be carried over to another. Recent work on partial transportability. EN.
course_use: Conceptual grounding for transferring test results between countries; his data-fusion tutorial videos suit advanced or PhD students; a guest talk is unlikely.

title: Armin Falk
author_source: University of Bonn and briq Institute on Behavior and Inequality, Professor of Economics; academic; DACH
note: Lead author of the Global Preference Survey (QJE 2018): experimentally validated measures of patience, risk, reciprocity, altruism and trust for about 80,000 people in 76 countries, with public data. Useful for explaining why treatment effects differ across markets. DE/EN.
course_use: Students can use the free GPS data to state hypotheses about cross-country differences in test effects; possible German or English guest talk (Bonn, remote).

title: Matthias Sutter
author_source: Director, Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods, Bonn; professor at Universities of Cologne and Innsbruck; academic; DACH (Austrian)
note: Experimental economist with lab and field experiments in Austria, Germany and abroad; widely read German-language books on behavioural economics; regular in Austrian media. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Strong German-speaking guest-speaker option with an Austrian link on experimental methods and behavioural effects; on site in Vienna or remote; German or English.

title: Michael Kirchler
author_source: University of Innsbruck, Professor of Finance; academic; Österreich
note: Co-author of large replication projects of experiments in Nature and Science (2016, 2018) and of many-designs and many-analysts studies showing how much results vary with design choices. Relevant for the robustness and replicability of experiments. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Austrian guest speaker on replication and design heterogeneity; Innsbruck, so remote or one-off on site; German or English.

title: Jean-Robert Tyran
author_source: University of Vienna, Professor of Economics, Vienna Center for Experimental Economics (VCEE); academic; Wien
note: Experimental economist, member of Academia Europaea, frequent commentator in Austrian media; VCEE runs the experimental lab at Uni Wien and a seminar series. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Local Vienna guest speaker on lab versus field experiments and behavioural results; possible lab visit for students; German or English.

title: Bernadette Kamleitner
author_source: WU Vienna, Professor of Marketing and Consumer Research and Vice-Rector for Research (since 2023); academic; Wien
note: Consumer psychologist doing experiments on privacy behaviour, such as people sharing friends' contact data with apps (international team, 2018) and privacy versus public health (2020). Relevant for consent, GDPR and the ethics of testing on users. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: In-house WU guest on privacy-aware experimentation and consumer consent; on site; German or English.

title: Bernd Skiera
author_source: Goethe University Frankfurt, Chair of Electronic Commerce; ERC Advanced Grant COOKIES; academic; DACH
note: Measures the economic effects of GDPR, cookie restrictions, consent walls, TCF and Apple ATT on online advertising; open-access book The Impact of the GDPR on the Online Advertising Market (2022); co-author with Klaus Miller on GDPR and online usage. DE/EN.
course_use: German-speaking expert for a session on how European privacy rules shape what can be tested and measured; remote or on site; German or English.

title: Avi Goldfarb
author_source: University of Toronto, Rotman School of Management, Professor of Marketing; academic; Global
note: With Catherine Tucker: Privacy Regulation and Online Advertising (Management Science 2011) used thousands of ad-effectiveness field tests across countries and found that the EU ePrivacy Directive lowered ad effectiveness in Europe. Classic cross-country comparison of experiment outcomes. EN.
course_use: Case for comparing ad tests across EU and non-EU markets; remote talk or recorded lectures (EN).

title: Jan-Benedict Steenkamp
author_source: UNC Kenan-Flagler, Knox Massey Distinguished Professor of Marketing; co-founder AiMark; academic; Global
note: Leading scholar of global marketing and cross-national consumer research (measurement invariance, global brands); books Global Brand Strategy (2017) and Brand Breakout (2013). Provides the theory for why marketing effects differ by country. EN.
course_use: Theory input for the international angle; recorded talks or a remote guest lecture on cross-national research design (EN).

title: Joseph Henrich
author_source: Harvard University, Professor of Human Evolutionary Biology; academic; Global
note: Coined WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) samples and ran economic games in many small societies, showing that behaviour measured in Western samples does not generalise. Book The WEIRDest People in the World (2020). EN.
course_use: Talk recordings and readings on cultural heterogeneity for the opening session; not a realistic live guest.

title: Nicholas A. Coles
author_source: Director, Psychological Science Accelerator (PSA); academic; Global
note: Leads the PSA, a distributed network of labs in more than 60 countries that runs the same experiment across countries (first study: 11,570 participants in 41 countries, Nature Human Behaviour). Shows how to set up a multi-country experiment. EN. Rolle prüfen; PSA founded by Christopher Chartier.
course_use: Remote guest on multi-country experiment logistics: translation, local adaptation, preregistration (EN).

title: Richard A. Klein
author_source: Lead of Many Labs 1, 2 and 4 (with Charles Ebersole, lead of Many Labs 3 and 5, and Brian Nosek); academic; Global
note: Many Labs 2 (Investigating Variation in Replicability Across Sample and Setting) ran 28 effects in about 125 samples from 36 countries and found little variation across settings for effects that replicate. A key counterpoint to assuming large cultural moderation. EN. Rolle prüfen (current affiliation not confirmed).
course_use: Use Many Labs 2 as a reading; remote Q&A on how cross-site heterogeneity was tested (EN).

title: Michael Hallsworth
author_source: Behavioural scientist, formerly Managing Director of the Behavioural Insights Team (BIT) Americas; Distinguished Lecturer, University of Pennsylvania; practitioner/academic; Global
note: Two decades of RCTs for governments and international organisations; author of A Manifesto for Applying Behavioural Science and The Hypocrisy Trap; experienced speaker. EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Remote guest on running behavioural experiments across countries and how BI units scale tests (EN).

title: Lucia A. Reisch
author_source: University of Cambridge, El-Erian Professor of Behavioural Economics and Policy (formerly Copenhagen Business School); academic; Global (German)
note: With Cass Sunstein, ran representative surveys in many countries on public acceptance of nudges (Trusting Nudges, 2019), showing country differences in what counts as acceptable intervention; consumer policy advisor to the German government. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: German or English remote guest on the ethics and cultural acceptance of behavioural interventions and tests.

title: Mårten Schultzberg
author_source: Spotify, Staff Data Scientist on the experimentation platform Confidence; practitioner; Global (Stockholm)
note: Co-author of Spotify papers on coordinating overlapping experiments (bucket reuse), sequential testing and risk-aware decisions with multiple metrics; co-host of the NerdOut@Spotify experimentation miniseries. Spotify tests across about 180 markets. EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Remote guest on running experiments in a global product with many markets (EN); podcast episodes as homework.

title: Nils Stotz
author_source: Zalando, Head of Product Experimentation; previously Contentful; practitioner; DACH (Berlin)
note: Leads product experimentation at a retailer active in about 25 European markets; presented Metrics for Experimentation Programs at XP 2025; spoke in 2025 at Experimentation Elite, Emerce Conversion and Analytics and Experimentation Unite. EN/DE. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Strong guest-speaker option for multi-market e-commerce experimentation; remote or on site from Berlin; English or German.

title: Melissa Li
author_source: Booking.com, Partner Hub Experimentation Lead (per AB Tasty case study); practitioner; Global (Amsterdam)
note: Case study describes prioritising test ideas by impact, evidence and ease, and running experiments across many languages and markets in the Booking.com partner app. EN. Rolle prüfen (vendor case study).
course_use: Remote guest or interview on localising tests across languages; pairs with the Booking.com HBS case (EN).

title: Ton Wesseling
author_source: Online Dialogue (Utrecht), founder and managing partner; founder and host of Conversion Hotel; practitioner; Global (NL)
note: Long-standing European experimentation consultant who has built testing programmes for multinational brands; promoter of evidence-based growth and experimentation maturity. EN/NL.
course_use: Remote guest on how agencies run test programmes for clients across European markets (EN).

title: Ruben de Boer
author_source: Experimentation consultant and trainer (Netherlands), winner of the Community award at the Experimentation Culture Awards 2025; practitioner/communicator; Global (NL)
note: Known for courses and content on experimentation culture and behavioural psychology in CRO; active community builder. EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Remote workshop on building an experimentation culture in international teams (EN).

title: Simo Ahava
author_source: Reaktor, Senior Data Advocate; analytics developer and blogger; practitioner/communicator; Global (Finland)
note: Leading European voice on Google Tag Manager, server-side tagging and Consent Mode; explains how GDPR and ePrivacy consent changes what is tracked in tests and analytics, and warns against consent circumvention. EN.
course_use: Blog posts and podcast episodes for the GDPR-compliant measurement session; remote talk possible (EN).

title: Aurélie Pols
author_source: Privacy engineer and data governance consultant (Mind Your Privacy); former DPO at mParticle; member of the EDPS Ethics Advisory Group; practitioner; Global (EU)
note: Digital analytics practitioner since 2001 who moved into privacy; speaks on GDPR readiness for analytics and data flows; taught privacy and ethics at IE Business School. Not a lawyer, which she states herself. EN/FR. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: Remote guest on privacy-by-design for experimentation and analytics stacks in Europe (EN).

title: Sinan Aral
author_source: MIT Sloan, David Austin Professor of Management; Director of the MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy and co-founder of CODE@MIT; academic; Global
note: Runs large-scale field experiments on social advertising and peer influence on global platforms; author of The Hype Machine (2020); co-founder of the Conference on Digital Experimentation. EN.
course_use: Recorded CODE@MIT keynotes and talks; a live guest lecture is unlikely.

title: Martin Spann
author_source: LMU Munich, Professor of Electronic Commerce and Digital Markets; academic; DACH
note: Pricing and digital-marketing field experiments, including pay-what-you-want pricing; research on online advertising and platforms in Germany. DE/EN. Rolle prüfen.
course_use: German-speaking guest on pricing experiments in DACH markets; remote or on site.

title: Psychological Science Accelerator (PSA)
author_source: Globally distributed network of labs in more than 60 countries; Global
note: Runs the same experiment in many countries with shared protocols, translation and preregistration; aims to fix reliance on WEIRD samples. The best template for multi-country experiment design.
course_use: Free membership for researchers; students can study published PSA protocols, and supervised theses could join a study as a collecting lab.

title: Many Labs replication projects (Center for Open Science / OSF)
author_source: Large crowd-sourced replication projects led by Klein, Ebersole, Nosek and others; Global
note: Many Labs 1 to 5 tested whether psychological effects hold across samples and countries; all materials and data are open on OSF.
course_use: Students reanalyse open Many Labs data to measure cross-site and cross-country heterogeneity; no sign-up needed to read.

title: Economic Science Association (ESA) and its meetings
author_source: Professional association for experimental economics; European Meeting 2026 at Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona (per UPF listing); Global
note: Main society for lab and field experiments in economics; regional meetings in North America, Europe, India and Southeast Asia; its journals are Experimental Economics and the Journal of the ESA.
course_use: PhD and master students can attend meetings (student fees) or follow programmes to find speakers; membership is paid.

title: Vienna Center for Experimental Economics (VCEE)
author_source: Core facility of the Faculty of Business, Economics and Statistics, University of Vienna; Wien
note: Runs the experimental economics lab and seminar series at Uni Wien; members publish lab and field experiments.
course_use: Students can sign up as participants in lab experiments and attend public seminars; possible lab visit as a field trip.

title: Insight Austria (IHS Behavioural Economics)
author_source: Behavioural economics competence centre at the Institute for Advanced Studies (IHS), Vienna, founded 2018; Wien
note: Austria's main behavioural insights unit: survey and field experiments for policy, training of civil servants in six ministries (Better Regulation in Austria). Team composition may have changed.
course_use: Contact point for an Austrian behavioural insights guest speaker (German); students can follow IHS events and job postings.

title: OECD Behavioural Insights Knowledge Hub and Network of BI Experts in Government
author_source: OECD Observatory of Public Sector Innovation (OPSI); Global
note: Map of more than 300 BI institutions in 63 countries, a project repository and a preregistration portal for experiments; the network has over 100 government officials from more than 50 countries.
course_use: Students browse the map by country to compare how BI units test interventions; free to view, registration needed to add projects.

title: Behavioural Insights Team (BIT) and Behavioural Exchange (BX) conference
author_source: Global behavioural science consultancy, part of Nesta; offices in the UK, Paris, Latin America and elsewhere; Global
note: Original nudge unit with thousands of trials in many countries; its BX conference (BX2025 in Abu Dhabi with about 500 experts) publishes recordings.
course_use: BX session recordings and BIT reports as material; BIT staff as remote guest speakers; newsletter sign-up is free.

title: Experimentation Elite
author_source: UK conference and awards for CRO and experimentation, London; Global
note: Conference with keynotes and moderated roundtables plus an annual awards evening (next listed: 24 September 2026, London); speakers include leads from Zalando and other multi-market firms.
course_use: Use speaker lists to find practitioner guests; tickets are paid and some recordings may be shared.

title: Berlin Experimentation Meetup
author_source: Practitioner meetup hosted by Marcel Toben and Patrick Gunia at Berlin tech firms (Babbel, Taxfix and others); DACH
note: Recurring meetup (10th edition 2025) with talks on causal decision-making and building experimentation culture at Berlin scale-ups that operate across markets.
course_use: Free sign-up on Luma; students can follow the group, and hosts and speakers are guest-speaker candidates; English.

title: Women in Experimentation (WiE) and WiE Summit
author_source: Community that began as a list of female experimentation speakers; summit co-run with Convert.com; Global
note: Two-day online summit (9 and 10 September 2026) with ten topics for experimentation, growth and UX professionals; the speaker list is a good source of diverse international speakers.
course_use: Free online registration; students can attend or watch replays; use the community to find speakers.

title: DDMA Experimentation Heroes Awards (Netherlands)
author_source: Dutch Data and Marketing Association awards for experimentation; Global (NL)
note: 2025 winners Odido, ANWB and PostNL in the Conversion, Beyond Web and Experimentation Culture categories; Dutch cases are some of the most mature in Europe.
course_use: Winners' cases as short examples; finalists as potential remote guests; information is free.

title: Kameleoon Who's Who in Experimentation (Continental Europe)
author_source: Vendor-curated directory of experimentation leaders, Continental Europe edition; DACH/Global
note: Profiles of experimentation leads at European firms with roles, talks and papers, such as Nils Stotz at Zalando. Vendor-curated, so selection is not neutral.
course_use: Use it to source DACH and European practitioner guest speakers; free to browse.

title: Samuel Goldberg
author_source: Marketing/economics academic, co-author of Regulating Privacy Online; academic; Global
note: With Garrett Johnson and Scott Shriver: GDPR reduced recorded EU page views and web revenue by about 12 percent across 1,084 firms (AEJ: Economic Policy 2024), separating real effects from data-recording loss. Key for understanding biased measurement in EU experiments. EN. Rolle prüfen (link is the paper, not a profile).
course_use: Reading plus possible remote talk on how consent gaps bias A/B test and analytics data in Europe (EN).

title: Scaling Reliable Experimentation in a Two-Sided AdTech Marketplace: ZMS Budget Split (Zalando)
author_source: Stefano Restelli and Carlos Garcia Alvarado, Zalando Engineering Blog, 2026, company tech blog post
note: How Zalando Marketing Services (retail media) tests advertiser-side changes when user-level randomisation breaks down because treatments share campaign budgets (interference). Budget Split gives each variant its own budget pool, and Orthogonal Concurrency lets several experiments run at once. Experiment volume rose from 8 (2023) to more than 60 (2025). No country-level results. Teaching question: why does a standard A/B test give biased results in a two-sided ad marketplace, and what is the unit of randomisation?
course_use: Example for a session on experiment design and interference (marketplaces, retail media); free.

title: Improving Efficiency in Offline Campaigns (Zalando gift-card campaigns tested across regions)
author_source: Martin Lawrence, Roman Romanchuk and Marc Bury, Zalando Engineering Blog, 2018, company tech blog post
note: Zalando gift cards sold through brick-and-mortar retailers and corporate benefit programmes. Store-level sales data let Zalando run offline campaigns as A/B tests across two comparable geographies, track their impact daily and steer them by ROI. No figures are reported. Shows how a geo split works for an offline channel.
course_use: Short example for geo-split testing of offline or partner channels; free.

title: Zalando Plus loyalty programme: live in Germany, piloted in Switzerland, then France and Italy
author_source: ChannelX (trade press), 3 May 2019, news article
note: Zalando Plus was available in Germany and was being piloted in Switzerland before planned roll-outs to France and Italy within twelve months. A later FashionUnited report (2023) puts it at more than two million members in six countries (DE, AT, FR, IT, NL, CH) before the Belgium launch. Teaching question: why use Switzerland, a smaller, higher-income, non-EU and multilingual market, as the pilot for a paid loyalty scheme, and what can it tell you about France or Italy?
course_use: Example of choosing a pilot country inside a multi-country roll-out; free.

title: Swarovski examined the relevance of generic search campaigns through geo experiments
author_source: Think with Google CEE (Google), case study (undated, c. 2019-2021)
note: Austrian brand Swarovski ran geo experiments in four key markets to measure the incremental value of generic (non-brand) search campaigns. It reports 2-3 euros of incremental revenue per euro spent, well above what last-click attribution had shown, plus more new customers. Published by the vendor, and the markets are not named in the snippet. Teaching question: why do generic keywords look worse under last-click attribution, and how does a geo experiment fix that?
course_use: Example for incrementality and geo experiments in a multi-country DACH brand; free, but the old URL now redirects to business.google.com/think, so check for an archived copy before class.

title: Swisscom: testing and personalisation with Adobe Target
author_source: Adobe, customer success story (vendor case study), English and other language versions
note: Swisscom's first tests (banner colours, CTA placement) produced an average uplift of 40% and won internal support for testing. It then moved to an Auto-Allocate (bandit-style) test of the default device shown on mobile product pages, and ran learning sessions to break down silos. Vendor-reported, with no baseline or sample sizes, so use it to discuss claims critically.
course_use: Example for building a testing programme at a Swiss telco and for scrutinising vendor uplift claims; free.
