title: AutoScout24 increased form conversion by 21.6% through experimentation
author_source: Optimizely, customer story (vendor case study)
note: AutoScout24 (Munich-based pan-European car marketplace) found in user research that buyers abandoned the dealer contact form because they did not know what to write. A test of a changed contact form raised form conversion by 21.6%. The company runs A/B tests on nearly every page. Example of research-driven hypotheses on a multi-country marketplace.
course_use: Short example linking qualitative research to an A/B test hypothesis; free. Our fetch returned 404, so check the URL before class.

title: HelloFresh scales to about 1,000 experiments per year with Statsig Warehouse Native
author_source: Statsig, customer story (vendor case study), c. 2025
note: HelloFresh's eight-person experimentation team moved from a slow in-house platform to a warehouse-native tool because most business metrics live in its data warehouse. Reported results: about 1,000 experiments a year, 25% less time to decision, and 55% more experiments reaching a decision. Vendor claims. Pairs with the HelloFresh experimentation-culture post already in the guide.
course_use: Example for experimentation scale and build-vs-buy decisions; free.

title: Democratizing Experimentation: How GetYourGuide Built a Flexible and Scalable A/B Testing Platform
author_source: Konrad Richter (GetYourGuide), PyData Berlin 2025, conference talk
note: The Zurich/Berlin travel marketplace moved from a centralised, closed experimentation system to a self-service platform where analysts and product teams define their own metrics and dimensions. Covers a Python Analyzer toolkit and open-source sequential testing code. Complements the GetYourGuide sequential-testing post already in the guide.
course_use: Example on democratising experimentation across many markets and teams; free (check for a recording).

title: N26 starts test phase in Brazil
author_source: The Paypers, 9 November 2021, news article
note: The Berlin neobank moved its Brazilian unit into beta, admitting about 2,000 of roughly 200,000 waitlisted applicants before the planned 2022 launch. Later reports describe gradual admission from a waitlist of more than 500,000. Teaching question: what can a small invited beta cohort tell a bank about product-market fit in a new country, and what can it not?
course_use: Example of a soft launch or beta in a new market (fintech); free.

title: Tencent-backed German fintech N26 launches in the UK (early adopters from waiting list)
author_source: CNBC, 4 October 2018, news article
note: N26 opened its UK app first to selected early adopters from a waitlist of more than 50,000, and held back features beyond the basic account until later. Pair with the Brazil beta and the 2015-2016 eurozone expansion to discuss staged market entry as a learning process.
course_use: Example for staged roll-outs and waitlist-based soft launches; free.

title: George, Erste's digital platform, in the final stretch in Romania (80/20 core vs. local features)
author_source: Wall-Street.ro, 28 February 2018, news article (Romanian)
note: Erste Group launched its George banking platform in Austria first, then in the Czech Republic and Slovakia at the same time, with Romania next. About 80% of the core is shared and 20% of features are local, partly because onboarding rules differ by country. In Austria the old and new systems ran in parallel for two years, while Slovakia migrated customers automatically. No formal tests are reported. Teaching question: how should a CEE bank sequence and localise a digital roll-out, and what should Austria teach it about later markets?
course_use: Example of a lead-market roll-out across CEE (Austria first); free. In Romanian, so use a browser translation.

title: Lidl accelerates roll-out of payment app (Lidl Pay pilot in Spain, then Denmark, Austria, Germany)
author_source: RetailDetail EU, 14 October 2019, news article
note: Lidl piloted Lidl Pay (QR-code payment inside Lidl Plus) in Spain from July 2019 and reported 70,000 app payments. Denmark and Austria were the next markets, followed by Germany. Example of a German retailer using a non-home market as the pilot for a digital service.
course_use: Example of pilot-country selection in retail; free.

title: Lidl Plus: digital loyalty card starts in pilot regions (Berlin and Brandenburg)
author_source: mobiflip.de, 12 June 2019, news article (German)
note: The Lidl Plus app was already live in other countries (Austria, Denmark, Poland, Spain according to other reports) when Germany got a regional pilot in about 250 Berlin and Brandenburg stores, initially Android-only, before the nationwide roll-out. Shows the regional pilot inside the home market as a variant of test marketing.
course_use: Pair with the Lidl Pay item for a discussion of international vs. regional pilots; free; in German.

title: Lidl startet neues Filialkonzept in Österreich (Metropolfiliale)
author_source: Leadersnet.at, 20 July 2017, news article (German)
note: Austria was one of the first Lidl countries to build the two-storey city-centre 'Metropolfiliale' (parking below, about half the usual floor space, full range). A Lebensmittel Zeitung report notes Lidl Switzerland was already rolling out a new store design while Germany was still testing it. Teaching question: why would a German retailer trial store formats in Austria or Switzerland?
course_use: Example of Austria/Switzerland as lead markets for store formats; free; in German.

title: Online-Geschäft: dm testet in Österreich taggleiche Lieferung
author_source: Manuela Ohs, Lebensmittel Zeitung, 2 May 2018, trade press article (German)
note: dm drogerie markt piloted same-day or chosen-date delivery in Vienna, with orders picked from store shelves, to learn how customers respond to flexible delivery. dm Austria had earlier run a test webshop (2013), and dm plans to launch online OTC medicines in Germany first and then Austria. Example of a German retailer using Vienna as a pilot city.
course_use: Example; paywalled (LZ subscription, WU-Lizenz prüfen); only the teaser is free; in German.

title: go2market expandiert nach Deutschland (market-research test supermarket from Vienna to Cologne)
author_source: Leadersnet.at, 1 March 2021, news article (German)
note: go2market opened in Vienna in autumn 2020: up to 1,500 members, matched to the Austrian population average, pay a monthly flat fee for EUR 55 shopping credit, and manufacturers get purchase data and survey feedback on new products. A first German store opened in Cologne in 2021. The Vienna shop later closed (vienna.at, 2022) because of supply problems and inflation, while Cologne continued. A modern, small-scale successor to the GfK Hassloch test market.
course_use: Example for test-market methods and their economics; free; in German.

title: Switzerland seen as top test market for Europe
author_source: swissinfo.ch, 30 December 2002, news article
note: Starbucks opened its first European store in Zurich (2001), and McDonald's tested its first Golden Arch hotels in Switzerland, with results deciding further expansion. The reasons given are an affluent, educated, multilingual population in a central location, and the US Commerce Department calls Switzerland an excellent test market for Europe. Teaching question: is Switzerland representative of Europe, and what external-validity problems follow?
course_use: Short reading for test-market selection and external validity; free.

title: From the archives: our first look at the Swatch (Texas test launch, 1982)
author_source: Europa Star, archive article (based on 1982 trade bulletin)
note: Before the March 1983 Swiss launch, ETA/Ebauches SA test-launched the Swatch in Texas in autumn 1982, with ads stressing style variety and ruggedness. Early buyers bought second and third watches in other colours, which led marketing to add new colours and styles regularly. No sales figures. A Swiss brand using a foreign test market. Pair with the INSEAD Swatch case.
course_use: Historical example of a cross-border test market; free.

title: Rund um die Uhr geöffnet: Migros startet Pilotprojekt mit einer Filiale in Herisau
author_source: SRF News, 3 July 2026, news article (German)
note: Migros Ostschweiz is piloting Switzerland's first 24-hour supermarket (300 m2, about 7,000 items): staffed until 19:00, then unstaffed with smartphone access and self-checkout. It builds on the unstaffed Teo stores (2022) and was delayed a year by an objection. Coop says 24-hour stores are not a topic for it. No evaluation criteria are published. Teaching question: what would a credible evaluation design for a single-store pilot look like?
course_use: Example for designing pilot evaluations (single site, no control); free; in German.

title: Migros tests small format Mio on SBB station sites
author_source: Immobilienbusiness.ch, 16 January 2026, trade press article
note: A temporary test of the 80 m2 'Mio' format at train stations (Baden, Zurich HB, with Bern, Birmensdorf and Islikon planned), after dozens of petrol-station sites, to see how commuters respond. Pairs with the Herisau 24-hour pilot to discuss staged multi-site format tests.
course_use: Example of a multi-site format pilot; free.

title: More leads and transactions: how VERBUND increases its conversion rate through A/B testing
author_source: e-dialog (Vienna agency), success story, 27 May 2026
note: Austrian energy company VERBUND ran 16 A/B tests over nine months on product detail pages, contact forms and homepage navigation. Transaction conversion rose by up to 15.8% and lead-inquiry conversion by up to 14.5%. Agency-reported, with 'up to' figures from the best variants. A rare documented Austrian corporate testing programme.
course_use: Example of a structured testing roadmap in Austria; free; good for discussing 'up to' uplift reporting.

title: How solving our biggest customer complaint at Blinkist led to a 23% increase in conversion
author_source: Blinkist (Berlin), UX Planet (Medium), c. 2018, practitioner article
note: Blinkist tested a transparent free-trial timeline plus a reminder before the trial ends, aimed at users who forgot to cancel. It reports 23% more trial conversions. Secondary write-ups add 55% fewer complaints and higher notification opt-in, but those figures are not confirmed in the original. A replication at another company (Clearful) found more trial starts but worse retention. Teaching question: ethical design, and choosing a primary metric when trial starts and retention diverge.
course_use: Example for paywall and ethics discussions; free (Medium; our fetch was blocked with 403).

title: Trivago test could prove big payoff for suppliers (auction slot test in select small markets)
author_source: Koddi, blog post (undated, c. 2019)
note: Trivago (Düsseldorf) tested fixed rules for its top four ad slots (direct hotel links, Express Booking, best rate with competitive CPC) only in select small markets before any site-wide change. No results reported. Example of using small countries as the testbed for marketplace mechanism changes, which also affects advertisers' CPC, CTR and CVR.
course_use: Short example of a market-level test of a marketplace mechanism; free.

title: Flixbus: how they boosted mobile app install rates across the globe
author_source: UserTesting / UserZoom, customer story, 19 July 2023
note: Flix (Munich) tested a redesigned app icon with surveys and click tests across countries it could not reach before, then confirmed the winner with A/B tests in Google Play store listings using larger samples. Shows a pipeline from qualitative research to an app-store experiment. No install-rate figures are given.
course_use: Short example of app-store A/B testing in international markets; free.

title: Why German e-commerce is optimizing in the dark (LEAP x SISTRIX analysis)
author_source: Tim Niemann, LEAP Digital Marketing, 10 August 2026, agency article (English and German)
note: Based on a LEAP x SISTRIX analysis (autumn 2025), around 73% of Germany's top online shops do not use an A/B testing tool. The article cites an average win rate of about 12% (Optimizely, more than 127,000 experiments) and 22-30% for mature programmes. Useful as a DACH baseline on testing adoption. The sample size is not stated and the source is an agency.
course_use: Context statistic for an opening discussion of testing maturity in DACH; free.

title: KONE: The MonoSpace Launch in Germany
author_source: Das Narayandas and Gordon Swartz (authorship per secondary sources), Harvard Business School, 2001, teaching case
note: Finnish elevator maker KONE test-marketed its new MonoSpace elevator in three European countries with mixed results, and its German subsidiary must now write the launch plan for Europe's largest market. MonoSpace had first launched as 'GreenStar' in the Netherlands. Directly about using test-market evidence from other countries to plan a German launch, including pricing and segmentation. B2B.
course_use: Case discussion on transferring test-market learning across countries; HBP paid (about USD 9-10 academic), WU-Lizenz prüfen. Product number taken from an HBP casemap, so verify the link.

title: Swatch
author_source: Christian Pinson and Helen Chase Kimball, INSEAD, 1990, teaching case (ref. 1853, 48 pp.)
note: Classic, award-winning case on the development and international launch of Swatch and its later line extensions. Use with the Europa Star item on the 1982 Texas test launch to discuss a Swiss firm testing abroad before its home launch. Experimentation is background, not the focus. The core is repositioning, the marketing mix and global vs. local advertising.
course_use: Case discussion, with test marketing as a side theme; INSEAD/Case Centre about EUR 7, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Lidl (Lidl US entry)
author_source: Jaan Elias and Ravi Dhar, Yale School of Management, 2025, teaching case (Yale Case 25-017)
note: Why Lidl has not repeated its European success in the US: it targeted 1,000 stores after its 2017 entry but had fewer than 200 and under 1% share by 2024. Decision point for the fourth US president on locations, assortment, CRM and value communication. Experimentation is not central. Use it for market-by-market learning, and ask what a staged test entry, such as smaller pilot stores, could have revealed earlier.
course_use: Case discussion on international market entry and learning; Yale online case, USD 9.50 per person.

title: Innovation and renovation: The Nespresso story (Revised)
author_source: Kamran Kashani and Joyce Miller, IMD, 2000, teaching case (IMD-5-0543, 24 pp.)
note: Nestlé ran Nespresso as a separate Swiss affiliate and grew it as a new niche, with the goal of going from CHF 150 million to CHF 1 billion. Other sources describe the background of the 1986 office-market launch in Switzerland, Italy and Japan, its underperformance and the pivot to households and the Club. The IMD page itself does not mention pilots, so experimentation is background only.
course_use: Case on learning from early market launches and pivots; IMD/Case Centre/HBP paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Foodora and Flash (A): Copycats Made in Germany
author_source: Michaël Bikard, INSEAD, 2025, teaching case
note: A Foodora co-founder (food delivery, modelled on Deliveroo, Rocket Internet orbit) decides whether to join 'flash', a micro-mobility venture modelled on Lime. The focus is imitation and competition, that is, transferring proven models across markets. Experimentation and testing are not central. Use it only to discuss what copying a proven model from one country to another does and does not de-risk compared with local testing.
course_use: Optional DACH start-up case; INSEAD about EUR 7, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Rocket Internet: The Start-up Factory
author_source: ICMR (IBS Case Research Center), c. 2016, teaching case (LDEN113)
note: The Berlin incubator replicated proven internet models (Zalando, Delivery Hero, HelloFresh and others) market by market around the world. The case covers its 2016 challenges after criticism of the model and falling valuations. Market-by-market roll-out is central. Formal experimentation is not. Use it to contrast 'copy and scale fast' with 'test and learn per market'.
course_use: Case discussion; ICMR paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen; our fetch returned 404, so check availability.

title: Marta Mijatov
author_source: A1 Telekom Austria AG, Digital Experimentation Lead; Wien; practitioner (Rolle prüfen)
note: Leads digital experimentation at A1, which won a 2024 Experimentation Culture Award; 20+ years in marketing incl. products, pricing and marketing plans across eight markets (multi-country angle). Named in Kameleoon's 2025 Who's Who in Experimentation; keynote at Kameleoon Unite Vienna 2026 on consumer psychology in experimentation.
course_use: Top Vienna guest-speaker fit: how a telco runs a test programme across markets; lecture or panel on site in Vienna; German/English.

title: Stephan Mühlbacher
author_source: A1 Telekom Austria, Digital Experimentation Scientist; Wien; practitioner (Rolle prüfen)
note: Co-presented the keynote 'Consumer Psychology: Hidden Driver for Customer and Business Success' with Marta Mijatov at Kameleoon Unite Vienna (22 Apr 2026). Data-science side of A1's experimentation programme.
course_use: Pair with Mijatov for a joint session (business plus statistics view); on site Vienna; German/English.

title: Jessica Volna
author_source: waterdrop (Vienna D2C brand), Senior CRO & Experimentation Manager; Wien; practitioner (Rolle prüfen)
note: Keynote 'Because We Think Isn't a Strategy' at Kameleoon Unite Vienna 2026 with Luke van Ravensberg. waterdrop sells in many European markets, so CRO across country shops is a natural topic.
course_use: Guest lecture on running CRO/experimentation in an international D2C e-commerce firm from Vienna; on site; German/English.

title: Luke van Ravensberg
author_source: waterdrop, E-commerce Manager; Wien; practitioner (Rolle prüfen)
note: Co-speaker with Jessica Volna at Kameleoon Unite Vienna 2026 on replacing opinion-driven decisions with tests in e-commerce.
course_use: Panel option alongside Volna; English likely.

title: Ekaterina Gamsriegler
